prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for adoption (hint, redesign), choose_path (copy, hint), finish (incentive, layout), and sign_in (copy, hint, notification, reorder) changes, as each has only 1 test so far.
finish new_screen changes have 2 tests agreeing that no clear effect was seen.
choose_path layout changes have 2 tests agreeing that no clear effect was seen.
home new_flow changes can be helpful since 1 test won, though 3 tests showed no clear effect.
No clear effect was seen for most changes tested so far (13 out of 18 tests).
Predictions generally overestimated impact for most tests, but underestimated the size of major wins.

Changes:
0: [finish, redesign] Desktop Pet Summon Redesign: Redesign the home intro page into a stage layout with an interactive mascot button prompting users to explicitly summon their pet onto the desktop. (why: Finish step has the lowest conversion rate (64.8%) and extremely high mean time (5815s), with support receiving multiple complaints that pets do not show up on desktop after setup.)
1: [choose_path, new_screen] Pet Archetype Quiz Screen: Insert a short choice quiz screen before path selection to help undecided users pick between quick preset selection and custom photo adoption. (why: The choose_path step has a mean duration of 514s vs median 8s, showing a long tail of indecisive users who stall during path selection.)
2: [finish, new_flow] Desktop Control Interaction Playground: Add an interactive desktop controls practice screen at the end of onboarding so users can practice dragging and interacting with their pet before completion. (why: 3 support tickets reported post-onboarding confusion regarding how to control, hide, or speak to the pet, contributing to high finish drop-offs.)
3: [home, wait_info] Desktop Generation Troubleshooting Tips: Display a tip carousel and reassuring text on the waiting screen explaining background pet processing and desktop display steps. (why: Waiting/home step has a huge mean duration (2336s) and support received tickets about custom pet generation failing or pets not appearing.)
4: [sign_in, layout] Single-Click Auth Compact Card Layout: Reframe the sign-in screen into a compact card layout with step counters to reduce visual friction and prevent stalling. (why: Sign-in mean time is 567s and support received bugs about sign-in screens stalling or failing to load.)
5: [adoption, copy] Adoption Certificate Name Confirmation Focus: Update adoption certificate copy to focus on naming the pet and confirming adoption in one step. (why: Adoption stage takes mean 1017s with dropoff to 74.3%, so clearer actionable copy can reduce hesitation.)
6: [finish, incentive] First Day Interaction Goal Badge: Add an explorer badge component on the home intro screen to motivate users to complete onboarding and unlock daily pet interactions. (why: Overall onboarding completion is only 24.7% and finish stage drops to 64.8%, showing a need for strong end-of-flow motivation.)

scores.note: Finish stage has the lowest completion rate (64.8%) and clear support complaints about pets not appearing, though layout/redesign builds require full release.
Adding new screens has shown no clear benefit in prior tests and choose_path lacks support email evidence.
High drop-off step supported by 3 tickets, but introducing interactive playground screens requires high effort.
Home step conversion is already high (87.4%), but high mean wait time and support tickets make lightweight copy/tips low cost.
Sign-in shows drop-offs and support tickets regarding stalling, with moderate layout effort needed.
Copy changes are fast and low cost (2), though evidence relies mostly on funnel time rather than support mail.
Previous finish incentive test yielded -1.7% relative change and lacks direct support mail alignment.
